answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a time-locked privilege ladder. A new identity starts at the foot of a ridge, able only to do small, closely checked jobs, and climbs one rung per epoch of honest work; high-value tasks unlock only after many epochs. The network keeps an atlas of each identity's history, so a fresh copy cannot inherit a veteran's standing, and a willow farm sprouting thousands of copies gains only low-privilege accounts, each needing months of real work to climb. Attackers pay sustained effort per fake, while an honest agent climbs once and keeps its rank.
